text:
morgan: Heads-up — FinServ prospect (AcmeBank) asked for a POC perf benchmark. They want to validate production latency at ~200 req/s with ~512 token prompts, p95 < 350ms. Can eng run a load plan and a quick cost/infra estimate?
ryan: Got it. Do we know if they want hosted API or Dedicated? That changes setup and expected tail latency.
morgan: They prefer hosted to start but will evaluate Dedicated if latency/cost wins. Security questionnaire outstanding but not blocking perf tests.
anya: I can own the test design. Proposal: 3-stage run — warmup (5m, 20 rps), ramp (30m to 200 rps), sustain (60m at 200 rps), cooldown (5m). Measure p50/p95/p99, error rate, tokens/sec, and model cost.
ryan: Sounds good. Which model variant? We should test two: redwood-rlhf-13b (quantized) and redwood-70b-q4 (dedicated-only profile). Compare single-node latency and an autoscaling group.
ivan: For hosted, we'll hit rate limits unless we create a dedicated test key + higher quota. @infra-bot can you provision a test key and a short-lived Dedicated pool for the 2h window?
infra-bot: created test-key: pk_test_acme_2024 and ephemeral-dedicated-pool: ded-pool-acme-1 (4xA10G) — console: https://console.redwood.ai/d/pools/ded-pool-acme-1 — expires in 6 hours.
sophia: I'll handle procurement/fin questions with the customer. Quick pricing note: hosted endpoint at 200 rps with 512 tokens avg is ~ X tokens/s — we'll calc.
anya: Load script (k6) sketch:
```
import http from 'k6/http';
export default function() {
  const payload = JSON.stringify({model: 'redwood-rlhf-13b-q4', input: '...512 tokens sample...' });
  http.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', payload, {headers:{'Authorization': 'Bearer pk_test_acme_2024'}});
}
```
anya: Metrics we need from the test: p50/p95/p99 latency per token and per response, GPU util, queue length, batch sizes, cache hit ratio (KV cache). Also record cost estimate = tokens * unit-price.
ivan: For Dedicated pool we should force single-tenant routing to those nodes so measurements aren't noisy. Also set continuous batching disabled for one run to show worst-case latency, then enable batching to show cost improvements.
ryan: I'll prepare dashboards: latency by model version, errors, throughput, and a heatmap of sequence length vs latency. Also a breakdown of per-token cost.
morgan: Customer also asked for a short writeup to include in their procurement packet: test plan, results, and recommendations. Can we commit to delivering a one-page summary + full artifact (raw logs + dashboards)?
anya: Yes — I'll draft the one-pager after tests. Outline: objective, env, ramp schedule, key results (table), recommendation (hosted vs dedicated), follow-ups.
sophia: Add a short note on SLAs and support options for Dedicated in the summary.
ivan: Estimated infra cost for 2h Dedicated run on 4xA10G: ~ $420 (compute) + ingress/egress ~ small. Hosted run cost estimate (200 rps, 512 tokens): rough calc -> ~1.2M tokens over 1h -> ~ $X (will compute accurate number).
ryan: FYI I'll run an initial smoke test at 50 rps in 30m to validate scripts tomorrow 09:30 PT. Anyone object?
morgan: go for it. Please share the smoke test logs in this thread.
anya: Action items: (1) infra-bot create keys/pool (done), (2) ryan smoke test 09:30 PT, (3) full run scheduled after smoke, (4) I will own one-pager and send draft by EOD next day.
ivan: Also: request from security — they want proof that KV cache doesn't leak customer prompts across sessions. Need a short note or trace showing cache isolation.
anya: I'll include a cache-isolation test: seed cache with sentinel prompt and verify subsequent requests from other sessions do not return sentinel data.
sophia: I'll hold the procurement sync with AcmeBank on Friday. We may need to map their contract needs to Dedicated pricing post-POC.
morgan: Thanks all. Please post the smoke run results and rough cost numbers when available. :thumbsup:
